findings.old_behavior: complete_check() (via ins_compl_check_keys) sets compl_interrupted = TRUE only when KeyTyped is set. Mapped typed keys lose the KeyTyped flag, so complete_check() returns FALSE for mapped input, causing the completion function loop to continue until the iteration limit.
findings.new_behavior: complete_check() (via ins_compl_check_keys) sets compl_interrupted = TRUE when KeyTyped is set, OR when in_compl_func is TRUE and reg_executing == 0 (not replaying a register). This allows complete_check() to return TRUE for mapped typed keys during completion, causing the completion function loop to exit early when the user types a mapped key.
findings.compatibility_reason: The complete_check() Vim function is a documented public Vimscript API. The patch changes its observable behavior: previously it would not return TRUE for mapped typed keys during completion; now it does (except during @r register replay). Vim plugins or scripts that call complete_check() to poll for user interruption will now observe earlier interruption when the user has mapped keys. This is an additive behavioral change that fixes a documented bug - the intended behavior was always to detect user input. The compatibility risk is extremely low because: (1) the change only makes the function work in more cases (additive), (2) any code depending on complete_check() NOT detecting mapped input was relying on buggy behavior, (3) the @r replay case is explicitly excluded.
findings.why_not_internal_only: ins_compl_check_keys() is an internal C function, but it implements the documented Vimscript function complete_check() (registered in src/evalfunc.c as f_complete_check). The behavioral change propagates directly to the public API: complete_check() now returns TRUE under conditions where it previously returned FALSE. This is externally observable by any Vim plugin or script calling complete_check().
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. The code change is small and well-understood. The only uncertainty is whether any existing Vim plugins depend on the buggy behavior (i.e., rely on complete_check() returning FALSE for mapped keys during completion). Such dependencies would be relying on a known bug.
findings.recommended_review: Review any Vim plugins that call complete_check() inside a custom completion function loop. If they rely on the loop running for a certain number of iterations (via sleep 5m or similar), the loop will now exit earlier when the user has a key mapping active. The fix is backward-compatible in all normal cases.
findings.test_recommendation: Run the existing test_ins_complete.vim test suite with focus on Test_complete_check_mapped_typed_key. Additionally, test mapped <Space> insertion during completion to verify the fix works and does not introduce regressions in other completion scenarios.
